title: tc-evaluation-dataset-editor
description:
An evaluation set's cases – input, expected output, checks, tags and split – in a windowed table with a case editor,
split counts and a comparison with an earlier version.

value.description: The set. Changed by the user unless a tc-value-change listener calls preventDefault()

splits.description: The splits a case can go in, in order – train, validation and test by default

assertionTypes.description: The kinds of check a case can have – contains, equals, matches schema and rubric by default

versions.description: Earlier snapshots of the set, oldest first, offered in the Compare select

compare.description: The id of the version to compare with, or "" for none. Changed by the user unless tc-compare-change is prevented

open.description: The id of the case open in the editor, or null. Changed by the user unless tc-open-change is prevented

description.description: A quieter line beside the heading, e.g. what the set tests

maxHeight.description: The table's height before it scrolls, in px

name.description: Submitted with the form: the set as JSON

disabled.description: Turns every control off and leaves the set out of the form; a disabled fieldset does the same

input.description: The prompt or input the model is given

expected.description: What a good answer looks like, if there is one

EvaluationAssertion.description: One check on a case's answer

EvaluationSplit.description: A split of the set: train, validation, test – or dev and test

description.description: A line under the check explaining what it does

multiline.description: The value is long text – a textarea instead of a one-line field

json.description: The value must be JSON (a schema, say) – text that doesn't parse is an error

EvaluationAssertionType.description: One way to check an answer: "contains", "equals", "matches schema", "rubric" – data, so an app can add its own

EvaluationDatasetVersion.description: An earlier snapshot of the set, to compare against
